report_name: APT28 Espionage Campaign Hits NATO Defense and Law Enforcement

threat_actors.name: APT28
threat_actors.description: A Russian state-sponsored threat actor, believed to be associated with Russia's GRU, that conducted a cyber-espionage campaign against high-value targets in two European NATO member states using the HOOKEDGE backdoor and a reflective loader.
threat_actors.goals: The primary goals of the campaign were credential theft and establishing long-term, covert access to the internal networks of the targeted organizations for intelligence gathering.

attack_patterns.name: Spearphishing Attachment
attack_patterns.description: Used macro-enabled Microsoft Word documents as the delivery vehicle for the HOOKEDGE backdoor.

attack_patterns.name: Visual Basic
attack_patterns.description: Malicious macros within Microsoft Word documents were used to execute code and initiate the infection chain.

attack_patterns.name: Process Injection
attack_patterns.description: A novel reflective loader was used to decrypt and execute payloads directly in memory to evade disk-based detection.

attack_patterns.name: Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
attack_patterns.description: The HOOKEDGE backdoor used webhooks for command and control communication, blending its traffic with legitimate web service APIs.

attack_patterns.name: Protocol Tunneling
attack_patterns.description: An SSH tunnel was established into the victim's internal network to provide persistent, encrypted, and covert access for data exfiltration and lateral movement.

attack_patterns.name: OS Credential Dumping
attack_patterns.description: Attackers used at least two distinct techniques to steal credential material from compromised systems.

malware.name: HOOKEDGE
malware.description: A backdoor used by APT28 that communicates using webhooks for C2, blending traffic with legitimate web service APIs. It has been previously observed in campaigns targeting entities in Romania, Spain, and Türkiye.

malware.name: APT28 Reflective Loader
malware.description: A previously undocumented reflective loader used by APT28 to decrypt and execute payloads directly in memory, evading detection by traditional security solutions. It required a key supplied at runtime.

tools.name: SSH
tools.description: Used by APT28 to establish a persistent tunnel into the victim's internal network for encrypted, covert access, data exfiltration, and further internal movement.

identities.name: Naval Shipbuilder
identities.description: A type of organization targeted by APT28 in a European NATO member state. The compromise aimed to steal intellectual property, ship designs, and naval technology.

identities.name: Military Aircraft Engine Manufacturer
identities.description: A type of organization targeted by APT28 in a European NATO member state. The compromise could lead to the loss of sensitive aerospace designs and performance data.

identities.name: National Law Enforcement Agency
identities.description: A type of organization targeted by APT28 in a European NATO member state. Access to its systems could expose ongoing investigations and compromise national security.

identities.name: North Atlantic Treaty Organization
identities.description: A political and military alliance whose member states' defense and law enforcement entities were targeted by an APT28 espionage campaign.

identities.name: GRU
identities.description: Russia's GRU military intelligence service, which is widely believed to be associated with the threat actor APT28.

infrastructure.name: HOOKEDGE Webhook C2
infrastructure.description: Command and control infrastructure used by the HOOKEDGE backdoor, which leverages webhooks to blend in with legitimate web service API traffic.

infrastructure.name: APT28 SSH Tunnel
infrastructure.description: An SSH tunnel established by APT28 for persistent, encrypted, and covert access into victim networks, used for C2 and data exfiltration.

indicators.name: Suspicious Process Creation from WINWORD.EXE
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Process Creation from WINWORD.EXE
id: 7e8b1c2a-3d4e-4f5a-8b9c-0d1e2f3a4b5c
status: experimental
description: Detects Microsoft Word spawning shell processes like powershell.exe or cmd.exe, which may indicate malicious macro execution.
references:
  - https://cypro.co.uk/insights/cyber-bulletins/apt28-nato-campaign-hits-defence-contractors/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-20
tags:
  - attack.t1566.001
  - attack.t1059.005
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\winword.exe'
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\cmd.exe'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects Microsoft Word spawning shell processes, a potential indicator of malicious macro execution as seen in the APT28 campaign.

indicators.name: Anomalous Outbound SSH Connection
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous Outbound SSH Connection
id: 1a2b3c4d-5e6f-4a7b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d
status: experimental
description: Detects anomalous or long-lived outbound SSH connections from non-standard clients, which could indicate SSH tunneling for C2.
references:
  - https://cypro.co.uk/insights/cyber-bulletins/apt28-nato-campaign-hits-defence-contractors/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-20
tags:
  - attack.t1572
  - attack.command_and_control
level: medium
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    DestinationPort: 22
    Initiated: 'true'
  filter:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\ssh.exe'
      - '\scp.exe'
      - '\sftp.exe'
      - '\putty.exe'
  condition: selection and not filter
indicators.description: Detects outbound SSH connections from unusual processes, which could indicate the use of SSH tunneling for persistent access, a technique used by APT28.

indicators.name: Potential HOOKEDGE C2 via Webhook Services
indicators.pattern:
title: Potential HOOKEDGE C2 via Webhook Services
id: f0e9d8c7-b6a5-4f3e-8d1c-0b9a8f7e6d5c
status: experimental
description: Detects network traffic to known webhook services from non-developer workstations, which could indicate C2 activity from backdoors like HOOKEDGE.
references:
  - https://cypro.co.uk/insights/cyber-bulletins/apt28-nato-campaign-hits-defence-contractors/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-20
tags:
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.command_and_control
level: medium
logsource:
  category: dns_query
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    QueryName|contains:
      - 'discord.com'
      - 'hooks.slack.com'
      - 'webhook.site'
  filter:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\slack.exe'
      - '\Discord.exe'
      - '\chrome.exe'
      - '\firefox.exe'
      - '\msedge.exe'
  condition: selection and not filter
indicators.description: Detects network traffic to common webhook services from unusual processes, a potential indicator of the HOOKEDGE backdoor's C2 mechanism.
